'''Erich Bornberg-Bauer''' (born 1963 in [[Vienna]]) is an [[Austrians|Austrian]] [[biochemist]], [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical biologist]] and [[bioinformatician]].

== Life ==
Bornberg-Bauer studied biochemistry, physics and mathematics (1981–1991) at the [[University of Vienna]] and obtained a diploma in biochemistry (1992). He performed his doctoral research on evolutionary fitness landscapes of [[RNA]] and [[protein]]s in the group of  [[Peter Schuster (theoretical chemist)|Peter Schuster]], Institute of Theoretical Chemistry, University of Vienna, and received his [[Ph.D]] in 1995.<ref name="uni-muen-Bornberg">{{Cite web|date=28 February 2022|title=Website of Erich-Bornberg-Bauer|url=http://bornberglab.org/people/bornberg-bauer/}}</ref> He continued his academic career at the University of Vienna (Institute of Mathematics) as a university assistant (equivalent to assistant professor; 1994 – 1996). Thereafter, he worked at the [[German Cancer Research Center|Deutsche Krebsforschungszentrum]] in [[Heidelberg]] as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in the group of [[Martin Vingron]] on algorithms for [[sequence analysis]] (1996–1998), and subsequently as a project leader at [https://www.eml.org/english/company/ EML (European Media Laboratory) GmbH] (1998 – 2000; this department is now a part of [[Heidelberg Institute for Theoretical Studies]]). Since 2000, Bornberg-Bauer has been working as an independent academic researcher, first as a senior lecturer in [[bioinformatics]] at the [[University of Manchester]] (2000–2003), and then as a professor of [[Molecular Evolution]] and [[Bioinformatics]] at the [https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/ Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity], [[University of Münster]] (2003 – present).<ref name="uni-muen-Bornberg" /> Since 2018, he is a guest scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biology]] in [[Tübingen]].<ref name="MPI">{{Cite web|date=28 February 2022|title=MPI for Biology Tübingen, Department Protein Evolution|url=https://www.eb.tuebingen.mpg.de/nc/protein-evolution/staff/}}</ref> He has been a guest professor at [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]] and a visiting scholar at [[EMBL-EBI|European Bioinformatics Institute]].

== Research ==

Bornberg-Bauer's earlier research focused on the aspects of RNA and protein evolution, especially on the phenomenon of [[neutral evolution]], [[evolvability]] and [[Robustness (evolution)|robustness]]. Together with Hue Sun Chan ([[University of Toronto]]),<ref name="huesunchan">{{Cite web|date=2 March 2022|title=Website of Hue Sun Chan|url=http://biochemistry.utoronto.ca/person/hue-sun-chan}}</ref> he developed the concept of ''superfunnels'' on [[neutral network (evolution)|neutral network]]s, which describes how populations of functional polymers (such as proteins) [[Genetic drift|randomly explore]] the sequence space to find transition sequences (''switches'') to new networks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bornberg-Bauer |first1=E. |last2=Chan |first2=H. S. |date=1999-09-14 |title=Modeling evolutionary landscapes: Mutational stability, topology, and superfunnels in sequence space |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=96 |issue=19 |pages=10689–10694 |doi=10.1073/pnas.96.19.10689 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=17944 |pmid=10485887|bibcode=1999PNAS...9610689B |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cui |first1=Y. |last2=Wong |first2=W. H. |last3=Bornberg-Bauer |first3=E. |last4=Chan |first4=H. S. |date=2002-01-22 |title=Recombinatoric exploration of novel folded structures: A heteropolymer-based model of protein evolutionary landscapes |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=99 |issue=2 |pages=809–814 |doi=10.1073/pnas.022240299 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=117387 |pmid=11805332|bibcode=2002PNAS...99..809C |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wroe |first1=Richard |last2=Chan |first2=Hue Sun |last3=Bornberg-Bauer |first3=Erich |date=2007-05-01 |title=A structural model of latent evolutionary potentials underlying neutral networks in proteins |journal=HFSP Journal |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=79–87 |doi=10.2976/1.2739116/10.2976/1 |issn=1955-2068 |pmid=19404462|pmc=2645552 }}</ref> His work also showed that errors in a protein's sequence that arise during [[Translation (biology)|translation]] (phenotypic mutations), help to explore the sequence space more rapidly. This phenomenon, termed as the ''look ahead'' effect, dramatically increases the probability of a gene to acquire [[Epistasis|beneficial double mutations]].<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1186/1745-6150-3-18|title = The look-ahead effect of phenotypic mutations|year = 2008|last1 = Whitehead|first1 = Dion J.|last2 = Wilke|first2 = Claus O.|last3 = Vernazobres|first3 = David|last4 = Bornberg-Bauer|first4 = Erich|journal = Biology Direct|volume = 3|page = 18|pmid = 18479505|pmc = 2423361 | doi-access=free }}</ref> His research group at the [[University of Münster]] has been working on three main research topics.
